findings.headline: Removing the queue consumer binding will break all queue processing after deploy
findings.body: The diff comments out the `[[queues.consumers]]` block for `openclaw-jobs`. Cloudflare Workers require the consumer binding to be present in the worker's configuration (wrangler.toml) for the runtime to deliver queue messages to the worker. The comment claims the consumer is still active at the dashboard level, but that is not how queue consumers work — the binding must be declared in the deployed configuration. After this deploy, the worker will no longer be invoked for queue messages, breaking CI triage, PR reviews, and any other queue-driven jobs. The correct fix is to keep the consumer binding in wrangler.toml and resolve the "Queue already has a consumer" error differently (e.g., by using `wrangler deploy --no-consumer` or by ensuring the binding is idempotent).
